title: Use NVIDIA NeMo to Turn Agent Failures into Tests and Harness Fixes | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA presents a trace-to-evaluation loop (NeMo Compass finds failures in traces, NeMo Eval Author builds tests, a harness change is validated on dev and held-out tasks) using a Hermes enterprise assistant example. A Dassault Systemes engineering example reports malformed tool calls falling from 142 to zero, a 28% relative score gain and 35% fewer tool calls per run.

insights.claim: Agent reliability depends on prompts, tools, routing, memory, skills and control flow, not model tuning alone, so generic benchmark scores often fail to explain domain-specific failures.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Value in agent deployments shifts to harness engineering and observability tooling rather than model selection.
insights.locator: When you build an agent for your domain

insights.claim: One wrong tool call can derail a whole task, and the cause may be an unclear tool description, a routing rule or missing context in the harness.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Failure attribution requires trace-level tooling, creating demand for agent observability products.
insights.locator: The agent harness is the optimization surface

insights.claim: In the example, a Hermes enterprise assistant asked to draft a message with project updates also called send_message without user confirmation.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Illustrates real risk of unauthorized agent actions via MCP-connected chat, email and tickets.
insights.locator: The agent harness is the optimization surface

insights.claim: The fix was a one-paragraph SOUL.md system-prompt change stating that requests to draft authorize preparation only and that a token from a preparation tool does not establish user consent.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Shows a cheap prompt-level fix can address a safety failure, though harness changes may also be middleware or plugins.
insights.quote: It does not establish the user's consent to that action.
insights.locator: Change one part of the harness

insights.claim: NeMo Compass analyzes stored traces and evaluation evidence to produce a prioritized backlog of issues with supporting trace IDs, rather than requiring engineers to inspect each run.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is moving up the stack into agent observability and evaluation software that sits alongside its models.
insights.locator: NeMo Compass: Find what to fix first

insights.claim: NeMo Compass detected the send-without-confirmation issue across 42 traces by comparing agent actions against the expected-behavior rules in ETHOS.md.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Behavioral specs in plain files become the reference for automated agent auditing.
insights.locator: NeMo Compass: Find what to fix first

insights.claim: NVIDIA claims that on internal benchmarks over thousands of traces, the full set of Compass signals found anomalies a coding agent given a similar task missed.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Unquantified vendor claim with no benchmark details provided.
insights.locator: NeMo Compass: Find what to fix first

insights.claim: NeMo Eval Author gives coding agents such as Codex or Claude Code skills to generate Harbor or NeMo Gym evaluations plus verifiers, and can create evaluations before production data exists using ETHOS.md and tool definitions.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Interoperates with rival coding agents, so NVIDIA tooling is positioned as a neutral layer over third-party agents.
insights.locator: Build evaluations around real agent work

insights.claim: The blueprint combines NeMo Compass, NeMo Eval Author and NeMo Relay, runs Hermes in an OpenShell sandbox on Linux with Docker, and requires an NVIDIA API key from build.nvidia.com.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Onboarding path funnels developers into NVIDIA's hosted API and Brev launchable.

insights.claim: After the prompt change, development-set passes rose from 3/6 to 6/6 with tool calls falling from 10 to 6, and held-out passes rose from 4/6 to 6/6 with tool calls falling from 28 to 15.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Small sample (two tasks, three runs each) but shows both correctness and efficiency gains.

insights.claim: Changes should be accepted only if they improve both the development tests and a held-out set, and held-out cases must stay hidden from the coding agent proposing changes to avoid overfitting.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Applies ML train/test discipline to agent harness iteration, a key practice for reliable agent products.

insights.claim: Production evaluation suites often contain hundreds to a few thousand examples, far more than the four-task demo.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Indicates the scale of evaluation infrastructure needed in real deployments.

insights.claim: After the fix, rerunning Compass no longer flagged the send-without-confirmation finding but surfaced a new one where the agent found the answer yet failed to ground its response in retrieved evidence.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Agent optimization is iterative whack-a-mole, implying recurring tooling usage rather than a one-off fix.

insights.claim: In a car-door design example using Dassault Systemes' LEO Virtual Companion, Compass found the agent placing QueryModel arguments outside the options field, producing empty errors it could not recover from.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Shows agent failures in engineering simulation tooling stem from schema errors, fixable by validation.
insights.locator: Apply the optimization loop to an engineering agent

insights.claim: A validation step for misplaced tool-call arguments cut malformed tool calls from 142 to zero with unchanged accuracy and no regressions in remaining scenarios.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Concrete reliability gain from a deterministic guard rather than model change.
insights.locator: Apply the optimization loop to an engineering agent

insights.claim: The optimization loop ran overnight without human intervention for about 12 hours, yielding a 28% relative improvement in the door-design workflow's overall evaluation score and 35% fewer tool calls per run across six scenarios.
insights.speaker: Patrick Moorhead
insights.so_what: Fewer tool calls imply lower inference cost per task, though the results are vendor-reported.
insights.locator: Apply the optimization loop to an engineering agent
